title: Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

reading.body:
An AI-powered issue triage system for the Cline coding tool was vulnerable to prompt injection attacks from December 2025 to February 2026. Attackers could craft malicious GitHub issue titles that tricked the AI into running arbitrary commands. A second attack vector allowed poisoning of GitHub Actions cache to steal and replace publication credentials for package repositories including NPM and VSCode Marketplace.

The system was deployed without sufficient isolation between user input and command execution. A human reviewer checking AI-generated responses before they ran commands, or restricting the AI's access to sensitive credentials, would have prevented both attack paths. The tool had over five million installations, meaning a successful compromise could have distributed malware at scale.

It is not established whether attackers successfully exploited the vulnerability to publish malicious code, though evidence suggests an attempt may have occurred during the window it was open.

Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

summary:
Cline, an open-source AI coding tool used by millions of developers, contained a critical security vulnerability from December 21, 2025, to February 9, 2026. The flaw existed in an AI-powered issue triage workflow that automatically responded to GitHub issues. Researchers discovered that attackers could exploit a prompt injection vulnerability by crafting malicious issue titles that tricked the AI into running arbitrary commands. Additionally, attackers could poison GitHub's Actions cache by flooding it with data to evict legitimate entries and replace them with malicious ones, potentially stealing publication credentials used to push updates to extension marketplaces and NPM.

The vulnerability could have allowed attackers to publish malware to millions of developers worldwide, as Cline reported over five million installs. An attacker theoretically could have created a single GitHub issue to trigger a chain of events leading to compromised production releases across VSCode Marketplace, OpenVSX, and NPM. Security researcher Adnan Khan submitted multiple disclosure reports starting January 1st, 2026, but received no response. Cline fixed the vulnerability within one hour of public disclosure on February 9th by removing the AI workflows and updating their CI/CD practices. Evidence suggests someone may have attempted exploitation during the vulnerability window, though no malicious updates were confirmed.
